Dan hari ini, aku tidak hanya bangga dengan hasilnya… tapi aku bangga karena aku tidak menyerah.. Untuk setiap langkah, setiap jatuh, setiap bangkit…  terima kasih sudah menjadi bagian dari perjalanan ini. The Unfiltered Truth About Being a WFH Mom Hindi ito para sa perpektong desk setup. Hindi ito para sa matching mugs at aesthetic home office. Sa lahat ng WFH moms ngayon, especially the breadwinners, multitaskers, at “kaya ko pa” moms, we see you. Kasi eto ang madalas hindi napag-uusapan tungkol sa pagiging WFH mom: 👩‍💻 WFH is a privilege, pero pwede ring maging mahirap. Nasa bahay ka nga… pero sabay kang employee, nanay, taga-asikaso, problem-solver, at emotional support system. 📅 Flexibility is beautiful, pero discipline ang bumubuo ng routine. Walang office clock-in. Walang boss na nakaabang. Minsan, ikaw ang pinakamahigpit na boss sa sarili mo. 🤍 Presence is priceless, pero guilt is real. Kapag nagtatrabaho, guilty kasi kulang sa time. Kapag nagpapahinga, guilty kasi feeling unproductive. Moms… gets namin. Hindi lahat ng araw ay productive. Hindi araw araw may benta tayo. At okay lang iyon. May cold coffee. May messy room. May deadlines. May iyakan. (At hindi lang si baby minsan) Yes, walang commute, pero napuno ng ibang responsibilidad ang oras. Yung oras na natipid? Napunta sa pagiging mas present na mama. At oo, kumikita ka from home, pero may sakripisyo pa rin. Rejections. Revisions. Burnout. Slow seasons. Self-doubt. Ito ang totoong WFH life na hindi laging nakikita online. Pero ito rin ang totoo: Hindi kailangang perfect ang setup mo. Hindi kailangang “supermom” ka araw-araw. Kung bumabangon ka pa rin at sumusubok ulit para sa pamilya mo, you're doing better than you think. 💛 Belated Happy Mother’s Day sa lahat ng WFH moms. Lalo na sa mga tahimik na lumalaban araw-araw. Day 19 of my 30 Day Cycling Challenge ✅🚴🏽‍♀️ I’ve been keeping the intensity pretty low for this biking challenge and honestly, I think that’s what’s helped me stay consistent. A lot of people think you have to go hard every time you work out to lose weight, but that mindset can actually backfire. It leads to burnout, injury, and skipped workouts. What actually works? Consistency. Even though my rides aren’t super intense, I’ve been moving my body almost every day, building habits, and showing up. And THAT adds up more than people think. So if you’re starting your weight loss journey and feel like you’re not “doing enough” because your workouts are slow, steady, or short… I promise, you are. Don’t underestimate what consistency can do.  #fitnessjourney #weightlossjourney #weightlosstransformation #weightloss #weightlossmotivation #weightlosschallenge #cyclingchallenge

🥓🧀🍞 Carbonara Sourdough BREAD Taste Test 🍞 Bread Deficiency Disorder Episode 6 ✨ I always forget to add extra cheese to the top of the bread halfway through baking but next time!! A yummy savory loaf for anyone who wants to try 🥰. ✨ Save for your next bake 🔖 **Ingredients** • Bread flour 428g @King Arthur Baking kingarthurbaking  • Semolina 70g @Bob’s Red Mill bobsredmill  • 2 egg yolks • water1 330g • Water2  30g • Ripe starter 116.5 • Pink sea salt 11g @redmondrealsalt redmondrealsalt  • a crap ton of cheese and black pepper Rough Recipe Method 1. Autolyse for 1 hour: mix all flours, egg yolks, and water until no dry spots remain. Cover and rest. 1. Add starter, salt, and water2. Mix until medium gluten development. 1. Gently fold in the inclusion and perform one set of stretch and folds. It will not be fully incorporated. 4. Rest 30 minutes, then perform stretch and folds. Repeat for a total of 3 sets. 5. Bulk ferment until airy and expanded. At 78°F, this takes about 3–5 hours after the final fold. 6. Gently pre-shape and rest uncovered on the counter for 1 hour. 7. Final shape and place in a banneton. Cold proof overnight. Preheat oven to 425°F convection. Bake: Open bake — 20 minutes with steam, then 25 minutes without. Dutch oven — 20 minutes covered, then 25 minutes uncovered. #bread #sourdough #baking #recipe #carbonara

I decided while pregnant that I wanted to exclusively breastfeed for at least a year. And honestly? I was excited because social media made it seem like breastfeeding would make the weight just melt off. 😅 Sooo.. that was NOT my experience. I strength trained and ran literally up until the day I went into labor. One week postpartum, I had already dropped a lot of weight and was only about 12lbs above my pre-baby weight. Then came the reality. From weeks 6–12 postpartum, I kept exclusively breastfeeding, strength training, going on walks, eating healthy… doing everything “right.” At 12 weeks postpartum, I stepped on the scale and had somehow GAINED 15 pounds. I was devastated. I cried. I got angry. I felt so defeated because none of it made sense to me. So I made a deal with myself: I would keep showing up for my body… but I was done obsessing over the scale because I was not going to stop breastfeeding anytime soon. Months 4 and 5 postpartum honestly felt slow. I didn’t SEE much change, but my clothes started fitting better and I slowly started feeling stronger again. Now at almost 8 months postpartum, I’m FINALLY starting to see all those months of consistency adding up. And I still refuse to step on the scale with a 10 foot pole 😂 This is just my REAL experience with exclusively breastfeeding while trying to lose baby weight. For some women it falls right off. For others, hormones, hunger, stress, sleep deprivation, and breastfeeding make it a much slower journey. And if you’re in that season too… you’re not failing. 🤍 4 more months of breastfeeding and then maybe my body will remember she belongs to me too 😂 #postpartumjourney #postpartumweightloss #newmom #momfitness #exclusivelybreastfeeeding

Postpartum is more than “bouncing back”. It’s healing while still having to show up every day.It’s loving your baby deeply while quietly struggling mentally and emotionally at the same time. It’s exhaustion that sleep alone can’t fix. It’s feeling overstimulated, touched out, overwhelmed, emotional, anxious, or disconnected and still trying to be everything for everyone. And sometimes postpartum depression doesn’t look like what people expect. Sometimes it looks like constantly staying busy so you don’t have to sit with your thoughts. Sometimes it looks like irritability, brain fog, shutting down emotionally, feeling guilty for needing space, or not recognizing yourself anymore. Stress after having a baby is real. The mental load is real. The pressure moms carry in silence is real. Your body changed. Your hormones changed. Your routines changed. Your identity changed. Healing takes time…..physically, mentally, emotionally, and spiritually. If you’re in this season right now, give yourself grace. You do not have to have it all figured out overnight. You are allowed to start small. You are allowed to rest. You are allowed to ask for help. You are allowed to take care of yourself too. Recovery is not just about losing weight or “getting your body back.”It’s about slowly finding yourself again. One walk. One workout. One prayer. One deep breath. One good day at a time. #P#PostpartumrecoveryjourneyP#Postpartumhealingp#postpartummomO#OverwhelmedMomMentalHealthForMoms

Postpartum recovery… take 4.  Maybe this season feels harder than you expected too. Between motherhood, work, school, taking care of everyone else, and trying to keep up with life, it’s easy to lose the motivation to take care of yourself. Easy to keep waiting for the “perfect” time to start moving your body again, eating better, or feeling like you again. But the truth is… there is no perfect time. Monday EAT fit meal! When it comes to soup recipes, I LOVE a classic Leek and Potato Soup. It's simple and delicious. Leeks are highly nutritious allium vegetable  that offer significant benefits for your heart, gut, and immune system while being exceptionally low in calories. Part of the same botanical family as garlic and onions, they feature a much milder, sweeter flavor profile while packing a dense concentration of protective antioxidants, vitamins, and minerals. Leeks are an excellent source of prebiotic fiber, specifically inulin. This fiber feeds and nourishes the beneficial bacteria in your microbiome, optimizing digestion and reducing bloating. They contain the flavonoid kaempferol, which helps safeguard blood vessel linings. They also provide potassium to help regulate blood pressure and folate to prevent compound buildups linked to heart disease.  If you’re lucky enough you can forage your own leeks this time of year.  Most Potato & Leek soup recipes use flour as thickening agent- this recipe contains no flour.  Ingredients  4 cups chopped potatoes  2 cups chopped leeks  2 cups choice of milk  2 tablespoons butter  1 tsp celery salt  1 tsp black pepper  1 tablespoon ginger powder  Directions  Boil 3 cups potatoes & remove skin after boiling. Remove water & let potatoes sit.  Sauté 2 cups chopped leeks in 2 tablespoons of butter until softened & browned.  Mash potatoes with hand stick blender in same pot used for boiled. Once mashed add in and blend leeks and milk & spices. (If you like your soup less thick..add more milk to consistency you like).  Warm it up on stove top & serve! Looking for a healthier cookie with less sugar and more protein and fibre than most?  These peanut butter chocolate chip cookies are higher protein, sweetened with banana and no sugar! Added sweetener is optional! Since there are no eggs in this recipe - taste before you bake! Add more sweetener as needed. This recipe works with chick pea or red or white kidney beans.  Here’s the recipe - I bet no one will guess that  these cookies are made with beans!  * 1 x 15oz or 540ml can chickpeas or white or red kidney beans or navy beans rinsed and drained * 1 ripe banana  * ½ cup nut butter  * ⅓ cup powder sweetener (I used stevia)  * 2 teaspoons vanilla * ½ teaspoon baking soda * ½ teaspoon baking powder * ½ teaspoon salt & 1/2 - 1 cup stevia chocolate chips  Blend the beans so they are super smooth! It should look just like  cookie dough! Mix in all the other ingredients saving chocolate chips for the end and feel free to taste as you go! Add more sweetener if you think you need it.  You can drop these cookies by teaspoon or roll into balks & press flat with fork so they make a nice round cookie shape. Bake 350 for 15 minutes! Enjoy! They store well in freezer until needed. Let’s look at the way we Climb stairs! Are you tip toeing or heel stomping?  1. Tip-Toe Stair Climbing  When you climb stairs strictly on the balls of your feet, your heels never touch the surface. Forcing your body up via the toes turns your ankles and calves into springs, which builds localized endurance in the lower legs (calves).  Leaning forward shifts your center of gravity, causing your knees to track far over your toes and placing higher shear stress on the knee joints. It eliminates the impact of the heel, making it the preferred method for moving silently through a quiet house.  Consistently preferring to tip-toe up stairs can sometimes be a sign of tight Achilles tendons or just habit.  Heel-Stomp Stair Climbing When you place your entire foot flatly onto a step and push downward through the heel, you maximize your structural frame. Driving through the heel recruits the large muscles of your buttocks and hamstrings, providing more raw power for vertical lifting. The intentional weight-bearing impact (the "stomp") signals your skeletal system to stimulate bone growth and density, which helps slow down bone loss!  Stacking your weight directly over a flat foot protects the cartilage of the knee, making it highly recommended by experts for painful or arthritic joints. Pushing straight down with massive force transfers vibration directly into the floor structure, generating loud footsteps. I don’t know who was more excited to be walking outside again, me or Jasper. ❄️🦿🐾 #labrador #walking #rewalk #exoskeleton #spinalcordinjury

✨ 2025 ✨ What a year it has been. My year started with a dream come true. I opened Jenn’s Gym Neuro Fitness Centre. A charity and gym for people with neurological conditions and disabilities.  On my annual trip to NextStep Orlando I made the biggest improvement in my recovery journey by being able to stand and step with no harnesses!  I had several new experiences with trying sit skiing and driving a car for the first time since my injury.  On the 29th June we adopted a new furry family member called Jasper. After losing Charlie last year, the house just felt empty but we knew the right dog would come along when the time was right. Roll on summer and a very shy 6/7 month old rescue appeared and we just knew he would be the perfect fit. Over the last few months he has grown more confident in himself and shown off his quirky personality.  Throughout the year I’ve had the opportunity to share not only my story but also the story of Jenn’s Gym and I’m soo proud of everyone who has supported me and the gym. Thank you for an incredible year and roll on 2026. 🤸‍♀️👩🏼‍🦽‍➡️🚶🏼‍♀️‍➡️ #CapCut #2025recap #happynewyear #spinalcordinjury #recovery @Jenn’s Gym

Getting my last few workouts in before Christmas! 🎄💪🏼 We tried a new sit up to box exercise in this session. I laid flat on the plinth holding a weighted bar and had to sit up and hit the exercise ball with the bar. Each time I sat up the ball was moved to a different position. As you can see it was a lot harder than I was used to so I had to do sets of 5.  After sit ups I transferred to the total gym for some shoulder shrugs and dips. Shoulder strength is super important when you are a wheelchair user as you use them every day to get around.  These exercises are also similar movements to what I do when using the parallel bars or my crutches so it’s good to get used to the feeling of pushing down.  @Jenn’s Gym #jennsgym #spinalcordinjury #gym #quadriplegic #totalgym

From standing to stepping! 🤸‍♀️👩🏼‍🦽‍➡️🚶🏼‍♀️‍➡️ I’m feeling more confident in my upper body when I’m standing now and I know that if I wobble I can catch myself and whoever is with me won’t let me fall. Because of this I decided to try stepping in the parallel bars. As I have a high level injury, callipers or KAFO’s were never recommended for me but I found a pair of knee braces online that would give me just that little bit extra stability incase my legs buckled. I loved the feeling of standing in the braces and being able to attempt steps was amazing! I can’t wait to keep practicing and see if I can walk a full length of the p-bars!  #spinalcordinjury #recovery #standing #walking #quadriplegic

If 16 year old me could see me now! 🤸‍♀️👩🏼‍🦽‍➡️🚶🏼‍♀️‍➡️ After my spinal cord injury I was told that my legs would never become functional again but I did not believe that. Having an incomplete injury means that some signals are still going through so why not try and strengthen them? Through physiotherapy and exercise I have been slowly improving my muscle strength and regaining movement in my core and legs. At times standing seemed like a dream that I was unsure was going to happen again without the help of robotic technology but now a lot of my physio sessions involve standing with very little assistance at all. I still have a long way to go but I am soo proud of how much progress I have made and soo grateful for all the support from my physios, family, friends and people from around the world supporting and encouraging me on this journey. 💙 #spinalcordinjury #recovery #standing #quadriplegic #gymnastics

When I’m not practicing standing, I’m keeping my body fit and strong with different pieces of equipment at @Jenn’s Gym!  My favourite piece of equipment is the @NuStep recumbent cross trainer as it gives me a full body workout.  I love exercising out of my wheelchair so I get on the plinth  to do some shoulder presses and sit ups with the weighted bar. I also practice tricep lifts with yoga blocks as this helps strengthen my arms for transfers.  #jennsgym #spinalcordinjury #quadriplegic #nustep #exercise
I did extra balance work this week when we braced the wind for a quick walk outside in my @ReWalk Robotics exoskeleton 🦿 #spinalcordinjury #rewalk #exoskeleton #quadriplegic #balance

Week 2 on crutches! 🩼  I gave my hips a huge stretch by leaning backwards on my first stand. Sitting in a wheelchair all day can cause tight hips so being able to stand and stretch feels amazing. I then worked on my sit to stands to see how much added height I needed to be able to stand up with the crutches. It’s crazy how much harder it is to go from sitting to standing compared to just holding your standing position. It takes a lot more muscle power but I’m definitely getting stronger with each session.  My core balance is also improving as I’m not as wobbly this week.  #standing #crutches #progress #spinalcordinjury #recovery

Wooden jump boxes (commonly known as plyo boxes) are heavy-duty fitness platforms engineered for explosive vertical conditioning, agility routines, and lower-body strength training. This Plyometric box is a perfect build to your cardio when taking on box jumps, step-ups, dips, or negative jumps. Are your workouts too easy on the 12-in side? Simply rotate the box to add 2-in or 4-in, forcing you to jump higher and burn more calories. These boxes are constructed from high-quality wood and are built to last. No matter your weight, you can be confident that when you land your jump, this box will support you.  #jumpbox #wooden #gymjump #wooden #jumpon

TRX suspension training leverages gravity and your body weight to build strength, balance, and stability. Exercises are categorized by the target muscle group and can be adjusted for difficulty by changing your body angle relative to the ground. TRX Low Row: Facing the anchor, lean back with arms straight, then pull your chest toward the handles while squeezing your shoulder blades. TRX Chest Press: Facing away from the anchor, extend your arms in a plank position. Lower your chest toward your hands and press back up, similar to a push-up. TRX Bicep Curl: Facing the anchor, keep your elbows high and "on the table." Curl your hands toward your temples. TRX Tricep Press: Facing away, hold handles at eye level with straight arms. Bend elbows so your head moves between your hands, then press back. TRX Y-Fly: Facing the anchor, pull your arms back and up into a "Y" shape to work the shoulders and upper back.

A manual treadmill is a self-powered fitness machine that relies entirely on your movement to drive the belt. Unlike motorized models, it requires no electricity, making it highly portable and eco-friendly. Curved Manual Treadmills: Premium, heavy-duty machines built for high-performance running and HIIT. The curved surface responds naturally to your stride—moving forward accelerates the belt, while moving back slows it down. #manualtreadmill #gym#treadmill #affordabletreadmill #treadmill

An air bike (or fan bike) is a stationary exercise bike that uses a large fan to provide unlimited, variable air resistance for a full-body, high-intensity interval training (HIIT) workout. As you pedal faster or push harder, the resistance increases automatically. They are commonly used in CrossFit and home gyms for building cardio endurance and strength. Key Features and Benefits Total Body Engagement: Dual-action handles engage the arms, chest, back, and core while pedaling works the lower body. Unlimited Resistance: Resistance scales directly with your effort, making it ideal for both low-intensity recovery and intense HIIT. Low Impact: Offers a high-intensity cardio workout that is easy on the joints, making it suitable for rehabilitation and cross-training. #airbike #commercial #gymtok #crossfitgirl #gymbike

Weightlifting belts create intra-abdominal pressure to stabilize your spine and protect your lower back during heavy compound movements like squats and deadlifts. Choosing the right belt depends heavily on your training style, preferred material, and fastening mechanism. Bodybuilding style belts are most often used to provide a safety net for when the core muscles become fatigued at the higher rep ranges bodybuilders train to provide extra protection. #weightliftingbelt #powerliftingmotivation #weightbelt #onlinestore #gymequipment

Hook straps" most commonly refers to weightlifting hooks or cargo tie-downs, depending on whether you're hitting the gym or hauling gear. These are designed to bypass grip strength limits, allowing you to lift heavier by transferring the weight to your wrists. How They Work: A metal hook sits in your palm and curves under the bar, while a padded strap secures it to your wrist.Best For: Heavy "pull" exercises like deadlifts, barbell rows, shrugs, and lat pulldowns. #deadliftmotivation #hookstraps #weightlifter #heavyweight #heavylifting

Barbell pads are essential for cushioning your neck, shoulders, or hips during heavy lifting. Most options feature high-density foam and are designed to fit both standard and Olympic-sized bars. Functional Neurological Disorder (FND) is a real and life-changing neurological condition that affects how the brain and body communicate. Symptoms can include weakness, tremors, pain, fatigue, seizures, sensory changes, speech difficulties, and cognitive challenges, often varying from day to day. FND is not “all in the mind” and deserves understanding, compassion, and proper support. Raising awareness helps reduce stigma, encourages earlier diagnosis, and reminds those living with FND that they are not alone. #livingwithfnd #fnd #symptoms #chronicillness #fndawareness

Epileptic seizures are caused by sudden, abnormal electrical activity in the brain. These electrical disturbances can be detected on tests such as an EEG and may result from epilepsy, brain injury, infection, genetics, or other neurological conditions. Symptoms can include convulsions, loss of awareness, staring spells, muscle stiffness, or unusual sensations. Treatment often involves anti-seizure medications and neurological care. Non-epileptic seizures, including Functional Neurological Disorder (FND) seizures or psychogenic non-epileptic seizures (PNES), are not caused by abnormal electrical brain activity. Instead, they occur because of a problem in how the brain and body communicate and function. These seizures are real, involuntary, and can be triggered by stress, trauma, emotional overload, or other physical and psychological factors. Although they may look similar to epileptic seizures, EEG tests are usually normal during events. Treatment focuses on therapy, education, stress management, and retraining the brain-body connection rather than anti-seizure medication alone #chronicillnessawareness #epilepsy #nonepilepticseizure #fnd #seizures

Functional Neurological Disorder (FND) is a real and treatable neurological condition that affects how the brain and body communicate. One common symptom of FND is non-epileptic seizures (NES), which can look similar to epileptic seizures but are not caused by abnormal electrical activity in the brain. FND can impact movement, memory, speech, sensation, emotions, energy levels, and overall daily functioning. Symptoms are genuine, involuntary, and can be triggered by stress, trauma, illness, fatigue, or sensory overload. With the right support, medical care, therapy, education, and understanding, many people living with FND can improve their quality of life and regain confidence and control #fnd #seizures #nes #chronicillness #chronicpain

Chronic illness and chronic pain can affect every part of a person’s life, even when the struggle is not visible to others. Pain, fatigue, brain fog, flare-ups, and emotional stress can make daily tasks, relationships, school, work, and personal goals much harder. Many people living with chronic conditions push through challenges that others may never see, often needing extra patience, support, and understanding. Although chronic illness can feel isolating, no one should have to face it alone. With awareness, compassion, and community, we can remind one another that invisible pain is still real, every story matters, and together we rise #chronicillnessawareness #chronicpain #chronicillness #fnd #fndawareness

People with FND may experience symptoms such as weakness, tremors, seizures, pain, speech difficulties, memory problems, or changes in movement and sensation. These symptoms are not imagined or “all in someone’s head”, they are genuine and can be disabling. With understanding, support, education, and the right treatment, many people with FND can improve and live meaningful lives. Awareness matters because kindness, belief, and respect can make a powerful difference #fnd #chronicillness #fndawareness #symptoms #facts

Functional Neurological Disorder, also known as FND, is a real condition that affects how the brain and body communicate. For some people, FND can cause speech difficulties, making words come out slowly, broken, repeated, or sometimes not at all. These symptoms are not made up and can be frightening, frustrating, and misunderstood. With patience, understanding, therapy, and support, people living with FND can find their voice in many different ways.
